title: Thom class of a vector bundle
statement:
Work in the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ and $n\geq1$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $\pi:E\to B$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $r\geq0$ with zero section $z$ [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. To fix the dual convention, write
$$E=\mathbf V(\mathcal M)=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}\mathcal M),\qquad \mathcal F=\mathcal M^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_B}(\mathcal M,\mathcal O_B).$$
Thus $\mathcal F$ is the locally free module of vectors in the fibers; the algebra generator map $\mathcal M\to\pi_*\mathcal O_E$ is equivalently the tautological section $s_{\mathrm{taut}}$ of $\pi^*\mathcal F$. Its zero scheme is $z(B)$ and it is a regular section. Define the supported Thom class by the localized top Chern construction [thm-pur-localized-top-chern]:
$$\operatorname{thom}(E):=c_r(\pi^*\mathcal F,s_{\mathrm{taut}}):z_*A_B\longrightarrow A_E(r)[2r].$$
The twists and derived tensor are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed; def-weil-derived-tensor]. Applying compact-support direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] gives
$$\tau_E:A_B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_!z_*A_B\xrightarrow{R\pi_!\operatorname{thom}(E)}R\pi_!\bigl(A_E(r)[2r]\bigr),$$
where the first isomorphism is the inverse of the composition identification $R\pi_!Rz_!\cong R(\pi z)_!=\operatorname{id}$ [thm-sf-comp-composition], using $Rz_!=Rz_*=z_*$ for the closed immersion.

For $r\geq1$ put $\overline E=\mathbf P_B(\mathcal M\oplus\mathcal O_B)$, $H=\mathbf P_B(\mathcal M)$ and $q:\overline E\to B$, with projective bundles interpreted as relative Proj of the symmetric algebra [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry]. The complementary open is $E=\overline E\setminus H$. Applying $Rq_*$ to the localization triangle [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] and using the two projective-bundle decompositions [thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula] identifies its fiber with
$$R\pi_!A_E\cong A_B(-r)[-2r].$$
Under a local direct-sum decomposition into line bundles, the supported class is the cup product of the pullbacks of their Thom classes along the projections from the total space; cup product has the meaning of [def-pur-supported-cup]. For $r=0$, $E=B$, $z=\pi=\operatorname{id}$, the Thom class and $\tau_E$ are the identity and the product is the empty unit product; no projective bundle of rank $-1$ is used.

proof.text: Use the relative-spectrum convention of [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. On an affine trivializing open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $\mathcal M$, [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] identifies $E_U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and the generator map sends $e_i$ to $x_i$. The corresponding section of $\pi^*\mathcal M^\vee$ is $\sum_i x_i e_i^\vee$. If $e'=eG$ then $x'=G^{\mathsf T}x$ and $e'^\vee=e^\vee G^{-\mathsf T}$, so these local sections agree on overlaps. Its zero scheme is the augmentation quotient $R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)=R$, exactly $z(U)$. Successive quotients by $x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}$ are polynomial rings in the remaining variables, and multiplication by $x_i$ is injective, by comparison of polynomial coefficients. The resulting regularity is checked at points of the zero scheme, so also covers empty opens. The empty tuple for $r=0$ gives the identity zero scheme. These are local coordinate verifications, requiring no regularity or smoothness of $B$.

source.place: first paragraph: tautological section and its zero scheme; dual convention made explicit

proof.text: The projection is affine by its relative-spectrum description, hence quasi-compact and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. On the charts of Step 1 its algebra is generated by the finite list $x_1,\ldots,x_r$, so [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] makes it locally of finite type; quasi-compactness makes it finite type. The zero section is closed by [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section], and hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. In particular the schemes and morphisms have the finite-type domains required in [def-pur-conventions]. Apply [thm-pur-localized-top-chern] on $T=E$ to the rank-$r$ bundle $\pi^*\mathcal F$ and the regular section of Step 1: its displayed morphism is exactly the definition of $\operatorname{thom}(E)$. This uses the specified canonical Chern construction, rather than choosing an arbitrary element of a supported Hom group. For $r=0$ use the degree-zero unit class, namely the identity on $A_B$.

source.place: first displayed morphism: apply the localized Chern construction to the regular tautological section

proof.text: For a proper map the compactification with identity open gives $Rz_!=Rz_*$ by [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]; $z_*$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], so $Rz_*A_B=z_*A_B$. The constant sheaf $A_B$ is the comparison pullback of the degree-zero constant etale $A$-sheaf, giving its bounded-below etale-origin witness; the closed pushforward stays in that class by [thm-sf-comp-composition]. That theorem applies to $B\xrightarrow{z}E\xrightarrow{\pi}B$, and since $\pi z=1_B$ its composition isomorphism gives $R\pi_!z_*A_B\cong A_B$. Invert it and follow it by the image of the supported morphism under $R\pi_!$. This constructs the displayed $\tau_E$ with its specified source. No assertion that $\tau_E$ is invertible is needed here: that is the separate vector-bundle Thom theorem. At rank zero this composite is the identity, using the identity normalization of the composition isomorphism.

source.place: second displayed morphism: compact-support pushforward with the source identification supplied

proof.text: Assume $r\geq1$. Construct $\overline E$ and $H$ by [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry], whose properness assertion applies to both projections (for $H$, use $n=r-1$). On a trivializing affine base chart their homogeneous rings are $R[x_1,\ldots,x_r,t]$ and its quotient by $t$. The complement $D_+(t)$ has degree-zero ring $R[x_1/t,\ldots,x_r/t]$. Changes of the basis of $\mathcal M$ give the same substitutions in $x_i/t$ as for the affine bundle in Step 1, so these chart identifications glue to $E=\overline E\setminus H$. Homogeneous quotient by $t$ defines a closed immersion $i:H\hookrightarrow\overline E$. The twisting module on the Proj charts has transition functions given by ratios of degree-one coordinates; restricting these functions to the charts of $H$ gives $i^*\mathcal O_{\overline E}(1)=\mathcal O_H(1)$. These are coordinate constructions, not an application of the field-only hyperplane clause of the geometry node to a general base. Apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] at finite coefficients to $A_{\overline E}$, and then the triangulated functor $Rq_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. By [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] the first term is $R\pi_!A_E$ for this compactification; by [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] the third is $R(qi)_*A_H$. Thus obtain the triangle $R\pi_!A_E\to Rq_*A_{\overline E}\xrightarrow{\rho}R(qi)_*A_H\to R\pi_!A_E[1]$, with $\rho$ restriction.

source.place: paragraph beginning Explicitly: projective completion and the pushed localization triangle

proof.text: Put $C_a=A_B(-a)[-2a]$ and $S=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{r-1}C_a$. By [thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula], the middle and right terms of Step 4 identify with $S\oplus C_r$ and $S$, via the powers of their respective hyperplane Chern classes. The equality $i^*\mathcal O(1)=\mathcal O_H(1)$ from Step 4 and the pullback identity of [lem-pur-kummer-additivity] give $i^*h=h_H$; since pullback commutes with cup products ($v^*(\alpha\cup\beta)=v^*\alpha\cup v^*\beta$, with support the whole scheme, [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]), $i^*h^a=h_H^a$. By naturality of the adjunction defining the two decompositions, this identifies the restrictions of powers $0,\ldots,r-1$ with the corresponding powers on $H$. Hence $\rho$ has matrix $[1_S\ v]$ for a morphism $v:C_r\to S$, which need not vanish. Precompose with the automorphism $(s,c)\mapsto(s-vc,c)$ to replace this matrix by the projection $S\oplus C_r\to S$. Its derived fiber is $C_r$: using the cone model of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the cone of this projection, shifted by $-1$, is $C_r$ plus the shifted cone of $1_S$. The identity cone is acyclic directly: for its differential $(y,x)\mapsto(dy+x,-dx)$, a cocycle $(y,x)$ has $x=-dy$ and is the boundary of $(0,y)$. Thus the second summand is zero after localization at quasi-isomorphisms, giving the asserted fiber identification $R\pi_!A_E\cong C_r$. This is a computation of the object, not an unjustified identification of $\tau_E$ with an arbitrary generator.

source.place: third display: fiber of restriction, with its potentially nonzero top-column correction

proof.text: On an open where the module of vectors decomposes as $\mathcal F=\mathcal L_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathcal L_r$, write $E_i=\mathbf V(\mathcal L_i^\vee)$ and $p_i:E\to E_i$. The tautological section has these pulled-back rank-one tautological components. Any subset of their coordinates has zero scheme given by that subset of $x_1,\ldots,x_r$; the coefficient argument of Step 1 proves regularity after killing any previous subset. Thus these sections form a transverse direct sum. Property (L2) of [thm-pur-localized-top-chern] identifies each component class with $p_i^*\operatorname{thom}(E_i)$; property (L3), iterated, identifies their product with the total localized class. The operation is precisely [def-pur-supported-cup], and its associativity is supplied by [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]. The intersection of the component supports is $z(B)$, so its source is $z_*A_B$ and its twist and degree are $r$ and $2r$. For one component there is no iteration; for none it is the unit chosen in Step 2. All constructions here have finite coefficients; no integral or rational coefficient transport is assumed.

source.place: last paragraph: product formula under a local decomposition, with pullbacks and transversality explicit

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $E\to B$ be a
vector bundle of constant
rank $r$, with zero section $z$ and projection $\pi$. The
tautological section of $\pi^*E$ has zero scheme $z(B)$; its
localized top Chern class of [thm-pur-localized-top-chern] is the
supported class

$$
\operatorname{thom}(E):z_*\Lambda_B\longrightarrow\Lambda_E(r)[2r].
$$

Applying $R\pi_!$ defines

$$
\tau_E:\Lambda_B\longrightarrow R\pi_!\Lambda_E(r)[2r].
$$

Explicitly, with $\overline E=\mathbf P_B(E\oplus\mathcal O_B)$ and
the localization triangle of the open $E=\overline E\setminus \mathbf P_B(E)$, the two
[thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula] decompositions for the
$\mathbf P^r$-bundle $\overline E\to B$ and the $\mathbf P^{r-1}$-bundle $\mathbf P_B(E)\to B$ identify the fiber of the
restriction map with

$$
R\pi_!\Lambda_E\;\cong\;\Lambda_B(-r)[-2r].
$$

Under a local decomposition $E\simeq L_1\oplus\cdots\oplus L_r$ the
supported class is $\operatorname{thom}(L_1)\smile\cdots\smile \operatorname{thom}(L_r)$.
